hed: Supreme Court leaves USPS mail-ballot rule blocked for midterms
dek: The Supreme Court on Monday night denied the Justice Department’s emergency stay application in Postal Service v. California (No. 26A305), leaving intact U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani’s preliminary injunction that blocks the Postal Service’s Aug. 21 Ballot Mail for Federal Elections final rule — specialized envelopes, unique barcodes, and a Federal Ballot Mail Portal — from taking effect for the November midterms. An unsigned order said the government was unlikely to succeed on the merits and that equitable factors did not favor a stay. Justice Kavanaugh concurred, saying midterm application would be arbitrary and capricious for lack of implementation time; Justices Alito and Thomas dissented.

byline: Event summary from public reporting and named outlets

cl.body: Votebeat’s Tuesday write-through, Reuters’s Monday SCOTUS wrap, and CBS News cast the denial as locking in status-quo mail voting for November after states and election officials warned they could not rebuild envelopes and portal workflows before ballots already began mailing — with the unsigned majority finding the government unlikely to prevail against Talwani’s injunction and Kavanaugh separately concluding midterm enforcement would violate the APA’s arbitrary-and-capricious standard.

cr.body: The Washington Examiner’s Monday denial brief, Just the News’s SCOTUS report, and Justice Alito’s dissent (joined by Thomas) frame the stay denial as leaving a nationwide injunction in place despite Alito’s argument that some challengers lack standing, that ultra vires claims are a “Hail Mary,” and that USPS has broad statutory mail authority — while the dissent stressed the government’s interest in enforcing anti-fraud ballot-mail rules before November.

stack_blurb: SCOTUS denies DOJ stay; USPS mail-ballot rule stays enjoined for midterms.
seo_description: Supreme Court denied the DOJ stay in Postal Service v. California, leaving the USPS mail-ballot rule blocked for the 2026 midterms. Dual sourced frames.
